memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So Abram went to live near the great trees of Mamre at Hebron, where he pitched his tents. There he built an altar to the Lord. - Gen 13:18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter ends the way Abram's life keeps ending: with an altar. He settles at Hebron, pitches his tent, and builds a place to worship. Tent and altar again - the pilgrim's dwelling and the worshipper's response. Wherever Abram went, God got an altar.

Compare the two men in this chapter. Lot pitched his tents near Sodom; Abram pitched his tent and built an altar. Lot chose by what he could see; Abram worshipped what he could not yet see. Lot moved toward the city of sin; Abram moved toward God. Two men, two directions, two very different endings.

Notice that Abram builds this altar after God's promise, not to obtain it. He isn't bargaining with God or trying to earn the land. He worships because God has spoken. Worship is our response to grace received, never a payment for grace desired.

That pattern is worth carrying into your own life. When God speaks, when God gives, when God keeps His promises - build an altar. Mark it. Give thanks. Let your response to His goodness be worship rather than merely relief. Hebrews urges us to "continually offer to God a sacrifice of praise" (Heb 13:15). Wherever this week takes you, pitch your tent lightly, and make sure God gets an altar.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Is your first response to God's goodness worship, or just relief?
- Where do you need to build an "altar" of thanksgiving this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, wherever I go, let me build an altar to You. Make worship my response to Your goodness, not a bargain for Your blessing. You are worthy of my praise today.
Amen.
